newsitem.title: USA: Swift Energy boosts production forecasts.
newsitem.headline: Swift Energy boosts production forecasts.

text.p: Swift Energy Co said Monday recent drilling has materially added to the its production forecast for the second quarter and remainder of the year.

The company said it has drilled and placed on production its largest natural gas well to date in the Austin Chalk Trend. The Orsak 1-OL, a dual horizontal well, flowed at a rate of 35 million cubic of natural gas per day on a 7/16 inch choke with a flowing tubing pressure of 7,200 pounds per square inch.
Swift Energy is operator of the well and owns a 34.5 percent working interest.
Its venture partner in this area, Union Pacific Resources Group Inc, owns a 50 percent interest working with the remainder owned by other private parties.

The Orsak 1-OL is the latest well to be completed on their joint development acreage in the Giddings Field in Fayette County, Texas. Collectively, six horizontal wells have been drilled in the area in the past 16 months, with both companies currently drilling offset wells on the joint acreage.

President A. Earl Swift said, "This well in Fayette County, combined with our recent success in Washington County with the drilling of the Schwickert 1 well (reported March 19) has materially added to the company's production forecast for the second quarter and remainder of the year. Production from these wells, and potential drilling locations on undrilled acreage around both of these locations, strengthen the company's outlook for growth in reserves and production."

On April 10, Swift noted, it also began drilling its first well on its 52,000 acre block in Walker County, Texas. Also targeted for the Austin Chalk Trend, this exploratory well should add a new development area to Swift's current operations. This well, the Gibbs 1-H, is anticipated to be completed in early June.
